parts:
Extension observations now stay on this machine. The test site can still send synthetic health data to Fly, and the extension posts only to `http://127.0.0.1:8765/events`.

## Files

Created:

- `network trace/event_store.py` appends one JSON object per line to `network trace/events.jsonl`
- `network trace/local_api.py` listens only on `127.0.0.1:8765`
- `network trace/extension/manifest.json`
- `network trace/extension/background.js`

Changed:

- `network trace/classifier.py` returns structured findings, prints the same CLI report, then stores the event
- `network trace/collectors/tshark_collector.py`
- `network trace/collectors/mitm_collector.py`

The test page is still `demo app/index.html`. It was not moved.

## Stored event

{

    "timestamp": "...",

    "source": "tshark",          *# or "mitm" or "browser_extension"*

    "scheme": "http",

    "method": "POST",

    "host": "fly-analytics.fly.dev",

    "path": "/collect",

    "destination_ip": "66.241.125.201",

    "destination_port": 80,

    "content_type": "application/json",

    "initiator": None,

    "tab_id": None,

    "third_party": None,

    "request_type": None,

    "body": {"birth_control": "IUD"},

    "findings": [

        {

            "field": "reproductive_health.birth_control",

            "value": "IUD",

            "category": "reproductive_health",

            "severity": "HIGH"

        }

    ]

}

Missing values are `null` in the file. `birth_control` and `pregnancy_goal` are category `reproductive_health`. `symptom` is `symptom`. `user_id` is `identity`.

## What each collector can fill

| **Field**                                 | **tshark**                   | **mitmproxy**           | **extension**                         |
| :---------------------------------------- | :--------------------------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------ |
| Body                                      | Decoded HTTP body            | Decrypted request body  | Always `null`                         |
| Destination IP                            | IPv4 address from the packet | Upstream socket address | Always `null`                         |
| Content-Type                              | HTTP header field            | Request header          | Request header when Chrome exposes it |
| Initiator, tab, third-party, request type | `null`                       | `null`                  | From `webRequest`                     |
| Findings                                  | From the body                | From the body           | Empty, because the body is `null`     |

`third_party` is a plain hostname comparison. `localhost` versus `fly-analytics.fly.dev` is third-party. There is no public-suffix list.

## Run

Local API:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

python local_api.py

It prints `Listening on http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

HTTP collector, in another terminal:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

python collectors/tshark_collector.py

HTTPS collector, in another terminal. Leave it running and do not type into that window:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

mitmdump -q --listen-host 127.0.0.1 -p 8081 -s collectors/mitm_collector.py

Test page:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/demo app"

python3 -m http.server 3000

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

Load the extension at `chrome://extensions`: turn on Developer mode, choose Load unpacked, and select `network trace/extension`.

For the HTTPS button, turn the browser proxy on only after mitmdump is listening:

networksetup -setwebproxy "Wi-Fi" 127.0.0.1 8081

networksetup -setsecurewebproxy "Wi-Fi" 127.0.0.1 8081

Turn it off afterward:

networksetup -setwebproxystate "Wi-Fi" off

networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "Wi-Fi" off

Check the log:

tail -n 3 "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace/events.jsonl"

## Verification

All three paths wrote one line each.

- HTTP: tshark stored a `POST /collect` with the JSON body and four findings.
- HTTPS: mitmproxy stored the same body with destination `66.241.125.201:443`.
- Extension: a POST to `127.0.0.1:8765/events` was stored as `source: browser_extension`, even though the payload claimed another source. Initiator was `http://localhost:3000`, tab was `12`, and `findings` was empty. A bad JSON body returned `400` and was not stored.

The previous tshark and mitmdump processes were started before this change, so they were stopped for the test. Start them again with the commands above.

## Privacy boundary

`background.js` has one destination, `http://127.0.0.1:8765/events`. Requests to `127.0.0.1:8765`, `localhost:8765`, and `[::1]:8765` are ignored, so the extension does not record its own POST. `local_api.py` binds to `127.0.0.1` only and does not contact Fly.

## Manifest V3 limits

`webRequest` can see method, URL, initiator, tab, request type, and normal request headers such as `Content-Type`. It does not provide the destination IP. Request bodies are left `null` rather than using partial or unsupported body access. The service worker sleeps when idle and wakes for request events. Seeing outbound requests requires the `<all_urls>` host permission.

parts:
Extension observations now stay on this machine. The test site can still send synthetic health data to Fly, and the extension posts only to `http://127.0.0.1:8765/events`.

## Files

Created:

- `network trace/event_store.py` appends one JSON object per line to `network trace/events.jsonl`
- `network trace/local_api.py` listens only on `127.0.0.1:8765`
- `network trace/extension/manifest.json`
- `network trace/extension/background.js`

Changed:

- `network trace/classifier.py` returns structured findings, prints the same CLI report, then stores the event
- `network trace/collectors/tshark_collector.py`
- `network trace/collectors/mitm_collector.py`

The test page is still `demo app/index.html`. It was not moved.

## Stored event

{

    "timestamp": "...",

    "source": "tshark",          *# or "mitm" or "browser_extension"*

    "scheme": "http",

    "method": "POST",

    "host": "fly-analytics.fly.dev",

    "path": "/collect",

    "destination_ip": "66.241.125.201",

    "destination_port": 80,

    "content_type": "application/json",

    "initiator": None,

    "tab_id": None,

    "third_party": None,

    "request_type": None,

    "body": {"birth_control": "IUD"},

    "findings": [

        {

            "field": "reproductive_health.birth_control",

            "value": "IUD",

            "category": "reproductive_health",

            "severity": "HIGH"

        }

    ]

}

Missing values are `null` in the file. `birth_control` and `pregnancy_goal` are category `reproductive_health`. `symptom` is `symptom`. `user_id` is `identity`.

## What each collector can fill

| **Field**                                 | **tshark**                   | **mitmproxy**           | **extension**                         |
| :---------------------------------------- | :--------------------------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------ |
| Body                                      | Decoded HTTP body            | Decrypted request body  | Always `null`                         |
| Destination IP                            | IPv4 address from the packet | Upstream socket address | Always `null`                         |
| Content-Type                              | HTTP header field            | Request header          | Request header when Chrome exposes it |
| Initiator, tab, third-party, request type | `null`                       | `null`                  | From `webRequest`                     |
| Findings                                  | From the body                | From the body           | Empty, because the body is `null`     |

`third_party` is a plain hostname comparison. `localhost` versus `fly-analytics.fly.dev` is third-party. There is no public-suffix list.

## Run

Local API:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

python local_api.py

It prints `Listening on http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

HTTP collector, in another terminal:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

python collectors/tshark_collector.py

HTTPS collector, in another terminal. Leave it running and do not type into that window:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

mitmdump -q --listen-host 127.0.0.1 -p 8081 -s collectors/mitm_collector.py

Test page:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/demo app"

python3 -m http.server 3000

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

Load the extension at `chrome://extensions`: turn on Developer mode, choose Load unpacked, and select `network trace/extension`.

For the HTTPS button, turn the browser proxy on only after mitmdump is listening:

networksetup -setwebproxy "Wi-Fi" 127.0.0.1 8081

networksetup -setsecurewebproxy "Wi-Fi" 127.0.0.1 8081

Turn it off afterward:

networksetup -setwebproxystate "Wi-Fi" off

networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "Wi-Fi" off

Check the log:

tail -n 3 "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace/events.jsonl"

## Verification

All three paths wrote one line each.

- HTTP: tshark stored a `POST /collect` with the JSON body and four findings.
- HTTPS: mitmproxy stored the same body with destination `66.241.125.201:443`.
- Extension: a POST to `127.0.0.1:8765/events` was stored as `source: browser_extension`, even though the payload claimed another source. Initiator was `http://localhost:3000`, tab was `12`, and `findings` was empty. A bad JSON body returned `400` and was not stored.

The previous tshark and mitmdump processes were started before this change, so they were stopped for the test. Start them again with the commands above.

## Privacy boundary

`background.js` has one destination, `http://127.0.0.1:8765/events`. Requests to `127.0.0.1:8765`, `localhost:8765`, and `[::1]:8765` are ignored, so the extension does not record its own POST. `local_api.py` binds to `127.0.0.1` only and does not contact Fly.

## Manifest V3 limits

`webRequest` can see method, URL, initiator, tab, request type, and normal request headers such as `Content-Type`. It does not provide the destination IP. Request bodies are left `null` rather than using partial or unsupported body access. The service worker sleeps when idle and wakes for request events. Seeing outbound requests requires the `<all_urls>` host permission.

parts:
Extension observations now stay on this machine. The test site can still send synthetic health data to Fly, and the extension posts only to `http://127.0.0.1:8765/events`.

## Files

Created:

- `network trace/event_store.py` appends one JSON object per line to `network trace/events.jsonl`
- `network trace/local_api.py` listens only on `127.0.0.1:8765`
- `network trace/extension/manifest.json`
- `network trace/extension/background.js`

Changed:

- `network trace/classifier.py` returns structured findings, prints the same CLI report, then stores the event
- `network trace/collectors/tshark_collector.py`
- `network trace/collectors/mitm_collector.py`

The test page is still `demo app/index.html`. It was not moved.

## Stored event

{

    "timestamp": "...",

    "source": "tshark",          *# or "mitm" or "browser_extension"*

    "scheme": "http",

    "method": "POST",

    "host": "fly-analytics.fly.dev",

    "path": "/collect",

    "destination_ip": "66.241.125.201",

    "destination_port": 80,

    "content_type": "application/json",

    "initiator": None,

    "tab_id": None,

    "third_party": None,

    "request_type": None,

    "body": {"birth_control": "IUD"},

    "findings": [

        {

            "field": "reproductive_health.birth_control",

            "value": "IUD",

            "category": "reproductive_health",

            "severity": "HIGH"

        }

    ]

}

Missing values are `null` in the file. `birth_control` and `pregnancy_goal` are category `reproductive_health`. `symptom` is `symptom`. `user_id` is `identity`.

## What each collector can fill

| **Field**                                 | **tshark**                   | **mitmproxy**           | **extension**                         |
| :---------------------------------------- | :--------------------------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------ |
| Body                                      | Decoded HTTP body            | Decrypted request body  | Always `null`                         |
| Destination IP                            | IPv4 address from the packet | Upstream socket address | Always `null`                         |
| Content-Type                              | HTTP header field            | Request header          | Request header when Chrome exposes it |
| Initiator, tab, third-party, request type | `null`                       | `null`                  | From `webRequest`                     |
| Findings                                  | From the body                | From the body           | Empty, because the body is `null`     |

`third_party` is a plain hostname comparison. `localhost` versus `fly-analytics.fly.dev` is third-party. There is no public-suffix list.

## Run

Local API:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

python local_api.py

It prints `Listening on http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

HTTP collector, in another terminal:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

python collectors/tshark_collector.py

HTTPS collector, in another terminal. Leave it running and do not type into that window:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

mitmdump -q --listen-host 127.0.0.1 -p 8081 -s collectors/mitm_collector.py

Test page:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/demo app"

python3 -m http.server 3000

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

Load the extension at `chrome://extensions`: turn on Developer mode, choose Load unpacked, and select `network trace/extension`.

For the HTTPS button, turn the browser proxy on only after mitmdump is listening:

networksetup -setwebproxy "Wi-Fi" 127.0.0.1 8081

networksetup -setsecurewebproxy "Wi-Fi" 127.0.0.1 8081

Turn it off afterward:

networksetup -setwebproxystate "Wi-Fi" off

networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "Wi-Fi" off

Check the log:

tail -n 3 "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace/events.jsonl"

## Verification

All three paths wrote one line each.

- HTTP: tshark stored a `POST /collect` with the JSON body and four findings.
- HTTPS: mitmproxy stored the same body with destination `66.241.125.201:443`.
- Extension: a POST to `127.0.0.1:8765/events` was stored as `source: browser_extension`, even though the payload claimed another source. Initiator was `http://localhost:3000`, tab was `12`, and `findings` was empty. A bad JSON body returned `400` and was not stored.

The previous tshark and mitmdump processes were started before this change, so they were stopped for the test. Start them again with the commands above.

## Privacy boundary

`background.js` has one destination, `http://127.0.0.1:8765/events`. Requests to `127.0.0.1:8765`, `localhost:8765`, and `[::1]:8765` are ignored, so the extension does not record its own POST. `local_api.py` binds to `127.0.0.1` only and does not contact Fly.

## Manifest V3 limits

`webRequest` can see method, URL, initiator, tab, request type, and normal request headers such as `Content-Type`. It does not provide the destination IP. Request bodies are left `null` rather than using partial or unsupported body access. The service worker sleeps when idle and wakes for request events. Seeing outbound requests requires the `<all_urls>` host permission.

Extension observations now stay on this machine. The test site can still send synthetic health data to Fly, and the extension posts only to `http://127.0.0.1:8765/events`.

## Files

Created:

- `network trace/event_store.py` appends one JSON object per line to `network trace/events.jsonl`
- `network trace/local_api.py` listens only on `127.0.0.1:8765`
- `network trace/extension/manifest.json`
- `network trace/extension/background.js`

Changed:

- `network trace/classifier.py` returns structured findings, prints the same CLI report, then stores the event
- `network trace/collectors/tshark_collector.py`
- `network trace/collectors/mitm_collector.py`

The test page is still `demo app/index.html`. It was not moved.

## Stored event

{

    "timestamp": "...",

    "source": "tshark",          *# or "mitm" or "browser_extension"*

    "scheme": "http",

    "method": "POST",

    "host": "fly-analytics.fly.dev",

    "path": "/collect",

    "destination_ip": "66.241.125.201",

    "destination_port": 80,

    "content_type": "application/json",

    "initiator": None,

    "tab_id": None,

    "third_party": None,

    "request_type": None,

    "body": {"birth_control": "IUD"},

    "findings": [

        {

            "field": "reproductive_health.birth_control",

            "value": "IUD",

            "category": "reproductive_health",

            "severity": "HIGH"

        }

    ]

}

Missing values are `null` in the file. `birth_control` and `pregnancy_goal` are category `reproductive_health`. `symptom` is `symptom`. `user_id` is `identity`.

## What each collector can fill

| **Field**                                 | **tshark**                   | **mitmproxy**           | **extension**                         |
| :---------------------------------------- | :--------------------------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------ |
| Body                                      | Decoded HTTP body            | Decrypted request body  | Always `null`                         |
| Destination IP                            | IPv4 address from the packet | Upstream socket address | Always `null`                         |
| Content-Type                              | HTTP header field            | Request header          | Request header when Chrome exposes it |
| Initiator, tab, third-party, request type | `null`                       | `null`                  | From `webRequest`                     |
| Findings                                  | From the body                | From the body           | Empty, because the body is `null`     |

`third_party` is a plain hostname comparison. `localhost` versus `fly-analytics.fly.dev` is third-party. There is no public-suffix list.

## Run

Local API:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

python local_api.py

It prints `Listening on http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

HTTP collector, in another terminal:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

python collectors/tshark_collector.py

HTTPS collector, in another terminal. Leave it running and do not type into that window:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace"

mitmdump -q --listen-host 127.0.0.1 -p 8081 -s collectors/mitm_collector.py

Test page:

cd "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/demo app"

python3 -m http.server 3000

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

Load the extension at `chrome://extensions`: turn on Developer mode, choose Load unpacked, and select `network trace/extension`.

For the HTTPS button, turn the browser proxy on only after mitmdump is listening:

networksetup -setwebproxy "Wi-Fi" 127.0.0.1 8081

networksetup -setsecurewebproxy "Wi-Fi" 127.0.0.1 8081

Turn it off afterward:

networksetup -setwebproxystate "Wi-Fi" off

networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "Wi-Fi" off

Check the log:

tail -n 3 "/Users/aabatiyow/Documents/GitHub/TigerHacks26/network trace/events.jsonl"

## Verification

All three paths wrote one line each.

- HTTP: tshark stored a `POST /collect` with the JSON body and four findings.
- HTTPS: mitmproxy stored the same body with destination `66.241.125.201:443`.
- Extension: a POST to `127.0.0.1:8765/events` was stored as `source: browser_extension`, even though the payload claimed another source. Initiator was `http://localhost:3000`, tab was `12`, and `findings` was empty. A bad JSON body returned `400` and was not stored.

The previous tshark and mitmdump processes were started before this change, so they were stopped for the test. Start them again with the commands above.

## Privacy boundary

`background.js` has one destination, `http://127.0.0.1:8765/events`. Requests to `127.0.0.1:8765`, `localhost:8765`, and `[::1]:8765` are ignored, so the extension does not record its own POST. `local_api.py` binds to `127.0.0.1` only and does not contact Fly.

## Manifest V3 limits

`webRequest` can see method, URL, initiator, tab, request type, and normal request headers such as `Content-Type`. It does not provide the destination IP. Request bodies are left `null` rather than using partial or unsupported body access. The service worker sleeps when idle and wakes for request events. Seeing outbound requests requires the `<all_urls>` host permission.
